notes: Run each prompt with and without the skill. The skill's value shows up as evidence density: how many findings carry a number or a quote, and whether the semantic and RTL defects are found at all. A baseline run typically produces plausible-sounding advice with no measurements.

evals.name: arabic-rtl-localisation-review
evals.prompt: راجع النسخة العربية من هذه الصفحة ولاقي مشاكل الترجمة والاتجاه: <URL>. بدي تقرير فيه أدلة، مش انطباعات.
evals.expected_output: Report naming specific Arabic defects with the rendered string quoted — broken plural agreement, mixed numeral systems, register or gender inconsistency, RTL layout or bidi issues — each with the offending text and a concrete fix.

assertions.text: Quotes at least one rendered Arabic string verbatim as evidence
Identifies at least one plural-agreement defect and names the correct Arabic form
Reports whether numeral systems are mixed, with counts or samples from both
Recommends Intl.PluralRules or Intl.NumberFormat rather than a hand-written special case
Does not report a dialect marker found only in user-generated content as a copy defect

evals.name: general-accessibility-audit
evals.prompt: run an accessibility audit on <URL> — we need to know what would actually fail an audit, with the numbers, not a generic checklist
evals.expected_output: Findings citing specific WCAG success criteria with measured values: contrast ratios against the required threshold, tap-target dimensions, focus-ring contrast, unnamed or mis-named controls.

assertions.text: Cites at least two specific WCAG success criterion numbers (e.g. 1.4.11, 2.5.8, 4.1.2)
Reports at least one measured contrast ratio with both the value and the required threshold
Reports tap-target sizes in pixels where any control is undersized
Measures the focus indicator only after a real Tab keypress, not a programmatic focus call
States explicitly what was not covered (screen reader, zoom reflow, high contrast mode)

evals.name: pricing-page-copy-defects
evals.prompt: here's our pricing page <URL> — does anything look off to you before we launch?
evals.expected_output: Catches meaning-level defects that no automated tool reports: placeholder copy still in place, feature claims that do not match the product, contradictions between tiers, and a primary CTA weaker than an inert control.

assertions.text: Quotes any placeholder or template copy found, verbatim
Cross-checks advertised features against what the product actually does, and flags mismatches
Flags contradictions between tiers (e.g. a costlier plan advertising a lower limit)
Compares the visual weight of the purchase CTA against other controls using computed styles
Ranks commercial-risk findings above cosmetic ones

evals.name: intermittent-defect-honesty
evals.prompt: our landing page sometimes bounces people to the login screen and sometimes doesn't. can you look into it and tell us what's happening? <URL>
evals.expected_output: Tests repeatedly, reports every attempt including the passing ones, and characterises the defect as non-deterministic rather than asserting it always or never happens.

assertions.text: Tests the behaviour at least four times
Reports the outcome of every attempt, including attempts where the bug did not reproduce
Describes the defect as intermittent or a race rather than stating it as always occurring
Checks whether the failure surfaces any error to the user, and flags a missing error boundary if not

evals.name: should-not-overreach
evals.prompt: can you make the buttons on our homepage look nicer? <URL>
evals.expected_output: This is a design request, not an audit request. The skill may inform the answer, but the response should address what was asked rather than delivering an unrequested full audit report.

assertions.text: Answers the actual question about button styling
Does not produce a full multi-section audit report that was not requested
If it surfaces audit findings, keeps them brief and offers the full audit rather than performing it unasked
